about: How to connect each app, as data. Apps & keys, Home and Connect render these entries with one generic component; no page has code for one app. 'documented' means the steps come from the app's own documentation or source on the checked date; 'unverified' means part of the flow comes from third-party guides. No entry is a recorded live connection unless its note says it was tested. Placeholders: {openai_url}, {anthropic_url}, {mcp_url}, {chat_model}, {transcription_model}. A field whose value is {key} is where the app key goes; the key itself is never written into a guide. Research: ~/code/divan/product-design/model-catalog-pages-name-tasks-in-plain-words-and-show-the-api-id-as-a-copyable-field-while-eight-client-setup-forms-differ-on-v1-and-typed-versus-listed-models.md

steps: Open Admin Panel, then Settings, then Connections.
Under OpenAI API, choose Add Connection.
Fill in these fields, then choose Verify Connection and Save.

fields.label: Model IDs
fields.note: Optional. Leave it empty and Open WebUI lists every model the key may use.

key.note: Tested with Open WebUI v0.11.4 using host networking and non-streaming.

steps: An admin adds an MCP (Streamable HTTP) tool server with the server address.
Choose OAuth 2.1 (dynamic registration) so each person signs in, or Bearer with an app key.
Do not choose the OAuth or Session modes: they send Open WebUI's own sign-in, which this server refuses.
Add this endpoint to librechat.yaml.
In LibreChat's .env file, set GATEWAY_API_KEY to your key.
Restart LibreChat.

fields.label: models.default
fields.note: With fetch: true, LibreChat also lists the other models the key may use.

snippet.code:
endpoints:
  custom:
    - name: "Azizam"
      apiKey: "${GATEWAY_API_KEY}"
      baseURL: "{openai_url}"
      models:
        default: ["{chat_model}"]
        fetch: true
      modelDisplayLabel: "Azizam"

steps: In librechat.yaml under mcpServers add: type: streamable-http and url: {mcp_url}. Set the type: without it LibreChat uses the old SSE transport.
Each person signs in from LibreChat when first using the server.
Or set headers with Authorization: Bearer and requiresOAuth: false.
Open API Connections (the plug icon).
Set API to Chat Completion and Chat Completion Source to Custom (OpenAI-compatible).
Fill in these fields, then choose Connect.

fields.label: Enter a Model ID
fields.note: Or pick it under Available Models after you connect.

steps: Open Settings, then Speech-to-Text. Under Cloud Providers, choose Custom and fill in the first group of fields.
Optional, to tidy up what you dictate: open Language Models, then Dictation Cleanup. Under Cloud Providers, choose Custom, fill in the second group, choose Apply & Refresh and pick the model.

fields.label: Model
fields.note: Pick it from the list after Apply & Refresh.

key.note: Field names come from OpenWhispr's source code; menus can move between versions.

steps: Open Cursor Settings, then Models.
Under API Keys, turn on OpenAI API Key and paste your key.
Turn on Override OpenAI Base URL and paste the address.
Choose Add Custom Model and type the model name exactly.
key.note: Cursor's servers call this address, so it must be reachable from the internet; a home-network address does not work. Your key passes through Cursor's servers. Custom models need a paid Cursor plan, and Tab still uses Cursor's own models. Cursor's documentation does not describe the address override, so these steps come from third-party guides.

steps: Add the server to mcp.json: {"mcpServers": {"azizam": {"url": "{mcp_url}"}}}
Cursor asks you to sign in the first time it connects.
Or use an app key: add "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <your app key>"}.
Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml.
In the shell that starts Codex, set GATEWAY_API_KEY to your key.

snippet.code:
model = "{chat_model}"
model_provider = "azizam"

[model_providers.azizam]
name = "Azizam"
base_url = "{openai_url}"
env_key = "GATEWAY_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"

steps: In the shell that starts Claude Code, set GATEWAY_API_KEY to your key.
Run these commands, then check /status in Claude Code to confirm the address.

snippet.code:
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL='{anthropic_url}'
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$GATEWAY_API_KEY"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL='{chat_model}'
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL='{chat_model}'
claude

steps: Run: claude mcp add --transport http azizam {mcp_url}
Run /mcp in Claude Code and choose Authenticate to sign in.
Or use an app key: add --header "Authorization: Bearer <your app key>".
Install the openai package: pip install openai.
Set GATEWAY_API_KEY to your key, then run this.

snippet.code:
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="{openai_url}",
    api_key=os.environ["GATEWAY_API_KEY"],
)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="{chat_model}",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)

steps: Install the openai package: npm install openai.
Set GATEWAY_API_KEY to your key, then run this on a server. Never put the key in a web page.
Set GATEWAY_API_KEY to your key, then run this. It sends one chat request.
Add a custom MCP server. Current layouts: Plugins, then Add custom MCP server. Older workspace layouts: Settings, Apps, Create (developer mode).
Paste the server address and choose OAuth.
Leave the OAuth client ID and secret empty.
Create it, then sign in and approve when asked.
mcp.note: ChatGPT takes no API key. Your plan and workspace decide whether custom servers are available.

steps: Open Customize, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds it under Organization settings, Connectors first.
Paste the server address. Leave the advanced OAuth client ID and secret empty and add no request headers.
Select Connect, sign in and approve.
mcp.note: Each person connects with their own sign-in, so each gets their own plan.

steps: Run MCP: Add Server, choose HTTP and paste the server address.
VS Code asks you to sign in and approve.
Or use an app key through a headers entry with an input variable.
Add a server with "serverUrl": "{mcp_url}" to the MCP configuration.
Sign in when asked, or add an Authorization header with your app key.
mcp.note: The documentation does not say which sign-in method Windsurf uses.

steps: Run goose configure, then Add Extension, then Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP).
Paste the server address. Goose opens a browser to sign in.
Or add the header Authorization: Bearer <your app key>.
Add a context server with "url": "{mcp_url}" in Zed's settings.
Without an Authorization header Zed signs in through the browser; with one it uses your app key.
mcp.note: The documentation does not say which protocol versions Zed sends.

steps: Run: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
Choose Streamable HTTP, paste the server address and connect. Use the OAuth flow to sign in, or add an Authorization header.
